events.title: Julian Calendar Takes Effect
events.description: The Julian calendar, introduced by Julius Caesar, went into effect in the Roman Republic, establishing January 1 as the start of the civil year and a 365-day year with a leap day every four years.
events.significance: It standardized timekeeping across the Roman world and was the basis for the Gregorian calendar, which is still used globally.

events.title: Union of Great Britain and Ireland
events.description: The Acts of Union 1800 came into force, merging the Kingdom of Great Britain and the Kingdom of Ireland to create the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.
events.significance: It reshaped British and Irish politics for more than a century and shaped later debates over Irish home rule and independence.

events.title: Emancipation Proclamation Takes Effect
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation took effect during the American Civil War, declaring enslaved people in Confederate-held territory to be free.
events.significance: It made the abolition of slavery a Union war aim, enabled Black men to enlist in the Union Army, and paved the way for the Thirteenth Amendment.

events.title: Cuban Revolution Succeeds
events.description: Dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Cuba, and revolutionary forces led by Fidel Castro took control of the country.
events.significance: It established a communist government allied with the Soviet Union just 90 miles from the United States, shaping Cold War tensions including the Cuban Missile Crisis.

events.title: Euro Introduced
events.description: The euro was launched as an electronic currency for accounting and financial transactions in 11 European Union member states, with physical notes and coins following in 2002.
events.significance: It created one of the world's largest currency zones and marked a major step in European economic integration.
